# zBuild — Vision
> The North Star for zBuild — it steers how zBuild is built. The README distills it; the wiki references it; every pipeline run is steered by it.
## Intent
zBuild turns a delivery process into data — templates and plugins — so software is built the same disciplined way every time. We build zBuild the way zBuild builds: a minimal core, with all behavior plugin-delivered and template-composed. A good change is small, aligned to the spec, proven by a test, and wired into the live path — never scaffolding that looks finished but does nothing.
## Principles
- **Target-agnostic by contract** — zBuild builds *any* repository, not itself; the engine and plugins never assume the target's language, layout, or that zBuild is the target. Target knowledge lives in data — templates, config, per-repo overrides — never in code.
- **Spec wins over drift** — KEEPERS, ARCHITECTURE, and the ADRs are the source of truth; when code disagrees, the code changes, not the spec.
- **Small engine, behavior at the edges** — keep the core tiny; add capability as plugins composed in templates, never by growing the engine.
- **Safety is structural** — all model-bound text passes one redaction chokepoint; state is atomic and resumable; scope is governed at every boundary.
- **Models are data, not code** — selection flows through the router and config tiers; never hardcode a model name.
- **Prove behavior, then wire it** — every change ships a test that fails without it and connects to the live path; green-but-inert is a defect.
- **Fail closed, never silent** — gates block on real problems and say why; bounded cycles and recovery drive work to done.
- **Dogfood every change** — build zBuild with zBuild; if the pipeline can't ship it, fix the pipeline.

# Design: Per-dispatch stage timeout with orch-sequential retirement (#1801)

## Summary

**Goal:** Every dispatched `run` hook is killed at a per-stage time limit on every dispatch route (map, fanout, sequential strategy, cycle member, parallel-group member, roleless leaf, `always_run`). The `orch-sequential` backend, which silently discards the limit it is given, is retired.

**Context:** `plugin_hook_call` today runs the plugin subshell with no watchdog. Flat backend timeouts (`ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT:-300`) undercut long-but-valid stages and are the only kill mechanism in the three strategy files. `_runner_dispatch_always_run` times out via the stage's `router.timeout_s` (one-model-call budget), not a whole-stage budget. `_orch_local_collect_results` kills with a 0.5 s grace, far too short to let a hook flush partial results. `orch-sequential` falls back silently when the configured backend is missing.

**Decision:** Introduce `stage_timeout_s` as a new top-level scalar parsed by `core/pipeline/template.sh` alongside the existing `router.timeout_s`. Its three-tier precedence is: template `stage_timeout_s` > `ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S` > 5400 s (90 min). The per-dispatch watchdog lives inside `plugin_hook_call` in `lifecycle.sh`, armed only for the `run` hook: the plugin subshell runs under `set -m` in the background; a paired watchdog calls `zbuild_pg_kill` (TERM + 10 s grace + KILL) and writes `timed_out` via the existing disposition layer on expiry. Because all dispatch routes — map, fanout, sequential strategy, cycle member, parallel-group member, roleless leaf, and always_run — reach `plugin_hook_call`, the single watchdog covers every route. Strategy files drop `ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT` entirely — the per-dispatch timer is the only stage limit. `_runner_dispatch_always_run` is updated to read `_TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_*` (not `_TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_*`). `simple.yaml` gains `stage_timeout_s` on every stage at the values named in R-6. `_orch_local_collect_results` and `_orch_local_shutdown_pool` replace `_orch_local_kill_slot` with `zbuild_pg_kill` / `zbuild_pid_kill` (10 s grace). `orch_load_backend` removes all sequential fallbacks; `_orch_load_backend` defaults to `bash-parallel`; `sequential` / `orch-sequential` as aliases emit `orch.backend.misconfigured`. The `plugins/tool/orch-sequential/` directory, its tests, the capabilities golden, and its wiki page are deleted.

## Rule ABS — generic enumerated-set / absence-by-omission wisdom

Some closed sets in this repo break by OMISSION rather than by a stale token you
can grep: the breakage is a MISSING (or orphaned) line, not a changed one. When a
change grows, shrinks, or renames such a set, every enumeration of that set is
wrong by omission — yet there is nothing to grep for, because the defect is the
absent entry.

When a change touches a genuinely-closed, exhaustively-enumerated set in this
repo, design MUST include in scope every test or config that enumerates or COUNTS
that set. Because the breakage is an absence, do not trust a hardcoded list of
sites to stay complete — rediscover the sites each time (see "How to find them").

This principle is target-agnostic: it applies to any closed set, and it does not
presume the pipeline stage set is closed (per the ADR-047 tombstone above, it is
not). Use it for sets that are genuinely closed in this repo, declared here per
ADR-032 as this repo's domain-specific enumerations.

## How to find them

Enumeration/count sites are most often mock-plugin roster blocks (one call per
member) or literal counts of the set. Rediscover them with:

```
grep -rln '_make_plugin\|_make_role_plugin\|_make_verdict_plugin\|mock_plugin_factory' tests/
grep -rln 'stage\.complete\|plugin\.run\.start\|started .*UTC\|finished .*UTC' tests/

Every match that enumerates or counts a closed set you are changing belongs in
the design scope block. Re-run the greps each time — new enumeration sites arrive
with new tests, and the defect (a missing line) leaves no token to search for.

# Design: Per-dispatch stage timeout with orch-sequential retirement (#1801)

## Summary

**Goal:** Every dispatched `run` hook is killed at a per-stage time limit on every dispatch route (map, fanout, sequential strategy, cycle member, parallel-group member, roleless leaf, `always_run`). The `orch-sequential` backend, which silently discards the limit it is given, is retired.

**Context:** `plugin_hook_call` today runs the plugin subshell with no watchdog. Flat backend timeouts (`ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT:-300`) undercut long-but-valid stages and are the only kill mechanism in the three strategy files. `_runner_dispatch_always_run` times out via the stage's `router.timeout_s` (one-model-call budget), not a whole-stage budget. `_orch_local_collect_results` kills with a 0.5 s grace, far too short to let a hook flush partial results. `orch-sequential` falls back silently when the configured backend is missing.

**Decision:** Introduce `stage_timeout_s` as a new top-level scalar parsed by `core/pipeline/template.sh` alongside the existing `router.timeout_s`. Its three-tier precedence is: template `stage_timeout_s` > `ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S` > 5400 s (90 min). The per-dispatch watchdog lives inside `plugin_hook_call` in `lifecycle.sh`, armed only for the `run` hook: the plugin subshell runs in a background subshell; a paired watchdog calls `zbuild_pg_kill` (TERM + 10 s grace + KILL) and writes `timed_out` via the existing disposition layer on expiry. The subshell isolation must not use `set -m` in the calling shell — the implementation must scope any job-control flag changes so monitor mode cannot leak into the runner shell after `plugin_hook_call` returns. Additionally, when the runner receives an external SIGTERM, the runner's signal handler must kill any isolated hook process group (not only the internal timeout path). Because all dispatch routes reach `plugin_hook_call`, the single watchdog covers every route and every backend. Strategy files drop `ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT` entirely. `_runner_dispatch_always_run` is updated to read `_TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_*`. `simple.yaml` gains `stage_timeout_s` on every stage at the values named in R-6. `_orch_local_collect_results` and `_orch_local_shutdown_pool` replace `_orch_local_kill_slot` with `zbuild_pg_kill`/`zbuild_pid_kill` (10 s grace). `orch_load_backend` removes all sequential fallbacks; `sequential`/`orch-sequential` as aliases emit `orch.backend.misconfigured` and return 1. `orch.backend.misconfigured` and `plugin.run.timed_out` are registered in `config/event-schema.json`. `plugins/tool/orch-sequential/` and all its files are deleted. `plugins/tool/orch-mock/plugin.sh` is updated so its `bash -c "$task_body"` dispatch closes stdin (`</dev/null`).

**SPEC-17 removed (tautology):**
The prior design's SPEC-17 asserted that orch-mock/plugin.sh exists — trivially true on both old and new code. The backend-agnostic property of the watchdog is structural: it lives in `lifecycle.sh` which is called by every backend. SPEC-1 already covers all dispatch routes and implicitly all backends. SPEC-17 has been removed; its backend-coverage rationale is absorbed into SPEC-1's description.

**SPEC-8 guard exclusion:**
`tests/unit/orch-backend-misconfigured-test.sh` mentions "orch-sequential" at line 6 in a historical commentary comment ("Before this change, orch_load_backend silently fell back to orch-sequential"). The guard must explicitly exclude this file from its grep, exactly as it already excludes `docs/adr/` and `tests/golden/`. SPEC-8 wording updated accordingly.

**SPEC-2 external-SIGTERM path:**
The watchdog's use of `set -m` (or process group isolation equivalent) places the hook subshell in its own process group. An external SIGTERM to the runner no longer propagates naturally to the hook's children. SPEC-2 is expanded to require that the runner's signal handler also kills the hook's isolated process group — covering both the internal timeout path and the external kill path (which `runner-release-exit-paths-test.sh` SPEC-6b tests).

**`set -m` leakage:**
The implementation at `lifecycle.sh:487` calls `set -m` in the calling shell. Any error path that exits before the matching `set +m` leaves monitor mode set in the runner shell, causing `runner-job-control-abort-test.sh` to fail. The implementation must ensure the `m` flag is never observable in the runner shell after `plugin_hook_call` returns — either by scoping the flag change to a subshell or by using a mechanism that does not touch the calling shell's flags.

- `core/pipeline/runner.sh` implements `_runner_dispatch_always_run` (SPEC-6/SPEC-10) and routes through the strategies; reverting it to today's code fails the always-run timeout test.
